title: Remembering what comes next
keyIdea: A routine is the same steps in the same order, every day. Think: what did I just do, and what comes next? Some steps must come first, like socks before shoes. The more you do a routine, the less you need reminders.

kid: Every day we wash our hands the same way. Wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry. That is a routine.
Think: what did I just do? What comes next? Soap is done, so now we rub.
Some steps must go first. Socks go on, then shoes. Shoes first will not work!
Do it every day. Soon you will know what comes next all by yourself.
adult: A routine is a short sequence of steps done in the same order each day: washing hands, getting ready to go out, snack time, bedtime. Remembering what comes next uses working memory, the part of thinking that holds a plan in mind, and it is an early part of executive function. Development Matters asks three and four year olds to be increasingly independent in meeting their own care needs, and steady daily routines are how that grows.

Picture routines help a lot. A now and next board shows the step happening now and the one after it, and a visual timetable shows a whole routine as a row of pictures. Use the same words each time: first, next, then, last. As your child learns the routine, take the pictures away bit by bit so they rely on memory, not reminders.

Common mistakes to watch for: thinking any order is fine, even when one step has to come first (socks before shoes, rinse before dry); skipping a step such as soap; and waiting for a grown-up to say every step. When a step is missed, ask what comes next rather than telling, and praise noticing a slip.

In the lab your child picks the next step on a now and next board for handwashing, builds the going-out routine in order, finds a missing step at bedtime, does snack time again with the pictures taken away, and spots where Pip swapped two steps.

familyTip: Take photos of your child doing each step of the morning or bedtime routine and stick them in a row by the door or the sink. Point and ask what comes next. After a week, cover one photo and see if they still remember it.

visual.caption: First or last? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: a now and next board, a going-out routine where order matters, a missing bedtime step, snack time with no pictures, and Pip's slip to fix.

practice.prompt: You wet your hands and put on soap. What comes next?
practice.hint: The soap is on. What do you do with it before you rinse?
practice.explain: Rub your hands next. Then rinse the soap off, and dry last.

practice.prompt: Mia gets ready to go out with {n} friends. Socks are on. What next?
practice.hint: What goes on over your socks?
practice.explain: Shoes go on next, over the socks. Then the coat, and then Mia and her {n} friends go out of the door.

practice.prompt: Bath, pyjamas, story, bed. Which step is missing?
practice.hint: What do you do before the story to keep your teeth clean?
practice.explain: Brush teeth is missing. It goes after pyjamas and before the story.

practice.prompt: Leo has done his bedtime routine {n} times. What happens as he does it more?
practice.hint: Does doing something again and again make it easier or harder?
practice.explain: After {n} times Leo needs fewer reminders. Doing a routine often helps you remember it.

pool.prompt: Pip puts on shoes, then socks. What went wrong?
pool.hint: Can socks go on over shoes?
pool.explain: Socks must go first. Shoes go on over the socks, so the order matters here.

pool.prompt: What is the last step of washing hands?
pool.hint: Think about the order: wet, soap, rub, rinse, and then?
pool.explain: Dry your hands is last. Wet hands is first, and soap comes second.

pool.prompt: A now and next board shows Now: sit down. What is Next at snack time?
pool.hint: Snack time steps are wash hands, sit down, eat, tidy up.
pool.explain: Next is eat the snack. After that you tidy up.

pool.prompt: Ava washes her hands {n} times today. One time she forgets the soap. What can she do?
pool.hint: Soap is the step that washes off the germs.
pool.explain: Go back and use the soap, then rub and rinse. Out of {n} washes, fixing one missed step keeps them all clean.

pool.prompt: Snack is eaten. What comes next?
pool.hint: Washing hands and sitting down came before eating.
pool.explain: Tidy up comes next. Wash hands and sit down came before the snack.

pool.prompt: What helps you remember a routine?
choices: Doing it the same way every day
pool.hint: Is it easier to remember something you do a lot, or something new each time?
pool.explain: Doing it the same way every day. The same steps in the same order soon stick in your memory.

pool.prompt: Sam puts on {n} things to go out. Coat, then door. What came before the coat?
pool.hint: Before the coat, you put on things for your feet.
pool.explain: Shoes came before the coat. Sam put on socks and shoes first, then the coat, then out of the door.

pool.prompt: Which words help you say the order?
pool.hint: Which words talk about what happens when?
pool.explain: First, next and last tell the order of steps in a routine.
